prepareCompensationMatrix

prepareCompensationMatrix.Rd

Prepares a compensation matrix for use with the compensate() function.

Usage

prepareCompensationMatrix(matrix, gs)

Arguments

matrix

A matrix or data.frame; the compensation matrix to prepare

gs

The GatingSet whose column names the compensation matrix's columns should be matched to

Details

For the flowWorkspace function compensate() to work, the column names (checked by calling colnames() on an object) of the GatingSet and compensation matrix must match. Oftentimes, by default, there will be minor name differences between these two objects e.g. two corresponding columns may be named BUV805-A and BUV805-A :: CD4 in the GatingSet and compensation matrix, respectively.

This function simplifies the process of matching and editing such column names by using substrings. In the example above, the compensation matrix column BUV805-A :: CD4 would search for a column in the GatingSet named either CD4 or BUV805-A, and be renamed to the match it finds.

An additional check that columns are in the correct order is done by ensuring that the compensation matrix's main diagonal contains only 1s.

Examples

# reading in compensation matrix
  comp_mat <- system.file("extdata", "auto_compensation_matrix.csv", package = "flowFun")
  comp_mat <- read.csv(comp_mat,
                       check.names = FALSE) # prevents column names from being edited

 # edit column names and reorder columns
  # not run: assume gs is a GatingSet
  prepareCompensationMatrix(comp_mat, gs)
#> Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)): error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'colnames': object 'gs' not found
